title: IB Spanish ab initio Common Mistakes to Avoid
summary: IB Spanish ab initio common mistakes can cost easy marks. Learn how to follow instructions, include evidence and units, and manage exam time.
body_markdown:
Some marks disappear because Spanish is difficult. Others disappear because a student answers the wrong question, omits a unit, copies too much evidence, or reaches the final task with four minutes left.


The most important **IB Spanish ab initio common mistakes** are preventable: misreading instructions, overlooking evidence or units, choosing the wrong text type, writing beyond your reliable language level, and managing time poorly. The solution is not simply learning more vocabulary. It is practising a repeatable exam process.


Consider a hypothetical student called Maya. She understands the texts and can communicate her ideas. Yet she loses marks after giving only *verdadero* without justification, writing *20* instead of *20 euros* , and using an informal message when the task requires a formal email. These mistakes do not reflect the full extent of her Spanish ability. That is why they matter.


### A quick mistake-prevention checklist


Before submitting an answer, ask:


- What exactly does the instruction require?
- Do I need evidence from the text?
- Have I included the relevant unit, person, place, or time?
- Is my evidence short, exact, and free from contradictions?
- Does my writing suit the audience, purpose, and text type?
- Have I protected enough time to check every section?


The[complete IB Spanish ab initio course guide](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/complete-guide-to-ib-spanish-ab-initio-course-details-assessment-tips-and-faqs) explains the wider assessment structure. Here, the goal is narrower: stop avoidable errors from consuming marks you could earn.


### Misreading the command or instruction


Maya sees *justifica tu respuesta* but notices only *verdadero o falso* . She chooses correctly and moves on. Her comprehension is sound, but her response is incomplete.


Words such as *identifica* , *indica* , *explica* , *completa* , and *justifica* specify what an answer must contain. A correct fact may still fail to satisfy the task when delivered in the wrong form. For a true-or-false item requiring justification, both the correct selection and valid supporting evidence are needed.


### Turn instructions into actions


Underline the operational word and translate it into an action:


Instruction Required action


*Identifica* Give the requested person, detail, or idea


*Indica* State the relevant information directly


*Completa* Supply only what completes the item


*Explica* Show how or why


*Justifica* Provide supporting evidence from the text


Build this habit through the[Spanish ab initio Questionbank](https://www.revisiondojo.com/ib/ib-spanish-ab-initio/questionbank) . Record instruction errors separately from language errors with RevisionDojo's[Mistakes Log](https://www.revisiondojo.com/features/mistakes-log) , since misunderstanding a task requires a different remedy from forgetting a verb ending.


A student presents an elaborate answer that does not fit the question


*An elaborate answer cannot rescue a misread instruction.*


### Missing evidence in reading answers


Maya understands why a statement is false but paraphrases the passage instead of selecting the required supporting words.


For true-or-false justification items, locate the shortest exact phrase that proves your decision. Do not copy an entire sentence merely because it contains the answer somewhere. Extra material can introduce contradictions or obscure the relevant evidence.


Use a simple routine: decide whether the statement is true or false, find the precise proof, and copy only the necessary words. The same discipline helps during[Paper 2 listening practice](https://www.revisiondojo.com/ib/ib-spanish-ab-initio/ib-spanish-ab-initio-paper-2-listening) , where identifying the requested detail matters more than recording everything you hear.


### Leaving out units and essential details


Suppose a question asks how much an activity costs. Maya writes *20* , although the text says *20 euros* . The number is present, but the meaning is incomplete.


Numbers belong to currencies, dates, times, distances, ages, prices, and durations. Treat the number and its label as one package: *15 euros* , *el 15 de junio* , *a las 15:00* , or *durante 15 minutos* .


Do not add a unit from assumption. Copy only what the passage or audio supports. Topic-based work in the[Spanish ab initio resource hub](https://www.revisiondojo.com/ib/ib-spanish-ab-initio) helps these distinctions become familiar before exam day.


### Choosing the wrong text type or register


In Paper 1, students complete two required writing tasks of 70-150 words each and select an appropriate text type from the provided options.


Before writing, identify the **audience** , **purpose** , and **text type** . A message to a friend should not sound like a request to a school director. An email needs a suitable greeting and closing, while a speech should acknowledge its audience. These conventions need not be elaborate, but they should be recognisable.


The[guide to earning a 7 in Spanish ab initio](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/how-to-get-a-7-in-ib-spanish-ab-initio) connects text-type control with wider exam preparation. RevisionDojo Study Notes and Flashcards can help you learn adaptable openings, transitions, and closings without memorising rigid responses.


### Writing Spanish that is too ambitious


One complicated sentence can create errors in tense, agreement, word order, and spelling. Prefer accurate, connected Spanish over fragile complexity. Linking secure sentences with *primero* , *además* , *sin embargo* , and *por eso* often communicates more effectively.


Use the[Spanish ab initio self-study resources](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/best-ib-spanish-ab-initio-resources-self-study) to organise recurring errors by tense, agreement, accents, register, and instructions. RevisionDojo's AI Chat and grading tools can explain why a construction failed, while Tutors can help address patterns that keep returning.


### Poor timing and unfinished tasks


Spending five extra minutes perfecting one answer may remove the chance to earn several accessible marks later. Divide your available time before starting, establish checkpoints, and reserve a final checking period. If one question stalls you, mark it and return later.


Untimed work builds understanding. Timed work builds exam behaviour. Use[Test Builder and Exam Mode](https://www.revisiondojo.com/features/test-builder) for targeted sets, then complete[timed Mock Exams](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/revisiondojo-mock-exams) to rehearse the full process.


### Turn preventable losses into a system


Improvement does not always require hundreds of new words. Sometimes it begins with reading each command, pairing numbers with units, choosing exact evidence, matching the text type to its audience, and following timing checkpoints.
